g.text: What temperature 0 really guarantees, why language models still give different answers
to identical requests, and how to make a finding reproducible enough to defend.
exercises ask you to edit them)
The story below is the setting. LANTERN is the local model; the case files are the text you send it.
The letter from Hale Brennan LLP arrives by courier at nine. Varma reads it standing up, then hands it
to you. "He is not wrong," she says, which is the most worrying thing she has said all week. "If LANTERN
gives two answers to one question, he will put both in front of a jury and ask them to pick. Find out
whether he can. Then make sure he can't."
First, these systems are known to give different answers to the same question. If your machine
produced one reading of a document on Tuesday and another on Wednesday, then neither reading is
evidence. It is a coin toss.
Second, I will ask for the exact instructions given to the machine, the exact model and the exact
settings used for every finding you rely on. If you cannot reproduce a finding on demand, in court,
I will ask the judge to exclude it.
: always take the most likely token
Greedy decoding. No randomness is drawn, so the seed does not matter. Five runs:
Deterministic is not the same as correct. A model can be reliably wrong.
. Same input, different numbers: what the server did before matters

Identical tokens in. When the server computes the whole prompt fresh it does the arithmetic in one shape;
when it reuses a cached prefix, in another. Floating point gives slightly different results for each, so the
. Why the shape of the arithmetic matters: floating point is not associative
A GPU adds up thousands of products in parallel, in an order that depends on batch size and kernel choice. A
different order gives a different last digit.
. When a last digit becomes a different answer
Two candidate tokens with almost equal scores:
picks the maximum. When two tokens are nearly tied, a rounding difference flips the winner,
and every token after it is written on a different path.

More detail: 'Try this' in lessons/06-temperature-zero-and-nondeterminism/README.md. Undo an edit with
git checkout <file>, or set every change aside with git stash.
Hale is half right. On this workstation, at temperature 0, the same question can come back with a
different total, because the server's arithmetic depends on what it computed just before. So LANTERN's
findings will be short, checkable readings, never sums, and each one is filed with a record: exact model
digest, server version, settings, prompt hash and output. The plate reading KB 714 FLR replays exactly
Varma signs the reply to Hale herself. "He asked for ordinary standards. He can have them."
